help:
nod bench [<dir>...] [--view available|active|decide|all|waiting|live|deferred]

  nod bench          opens every folder registered with nod projects, from anywhere
  nod bench .        opens only the project the current directory is in
  nod bench ~/Code/a ~/Code/b   opens only these (--dir also works)
  nod bench --json   everything bench shows — each view's rows, every node's detail — as one JSON object, for a window that draws it
  nod bench --json --node <id>   one node's detail, archived ones included
  nod bench --json --view <id> | --def '<json>'   one tab only, or a view not saved yet (nod view --help)


Tabs across the top: Available N / Active N / Human work N / Waiting N / Live / All (⇥ to switch, opens on Available).
  Available  what is moving now: running, waiting outside, startable, needing a decision, answered and awaiting an AI (tree, ancestors shown dim)
  Active     running, needing a decision, or any live human work (tree)
  Human work  what waits on you: decisions to make and your own to-dos, AI-blocking first, then ★
  Waiting    everything delayed (d, nod defer / nod hold): waiting on someone (purple) or put off to a day (grey)
  Live       every node that changed, by anyone, newest change first, finished ones too (h)
  All        every node; finished ones fold into "✓ Completed N" / "✓ Finished N", +/- expands
Old --view tree|owner|running|timeline|done still works (maps to the nearest view).
When there are external sources, a line under the tabs says whether they're clear. Left is nodes, right is the current one.
↑↓ picks a node, ←→ / +- fold/unfold, digits answer, Enter takes the default, w jumps to the next decision, g jumps by number, d defers/undefers, ? shows every key, , opens Settings.
Mouse works too: click a tab name, a node, an option, an attachment; the wheel scrolls whichever pane it's over.
Press o to view a screenshot right in the terminal (iTerm2 / kitty family; tmux swallows it,
set NODDIT_IMAGES=iterm with passthrough enabled).
Register folders with: nod projects add <dir> (nod init does this automatically); stored in ~/.decs/config.json.
With nothing registered, it falls back to walking up from the current directory for a decisions/ folder.

helpScreen:
Six tabs, ⇥ / ⇧⇥ to switch (digits are reserved for answering); opens on Available:
    Available  what is moving now: running, waiting outside, startable, needing a decision, answered
               and awaiting an AI; the project tree, with ancestors listed dim so you can see where
               a match hangs
    Active     what is actually happening: running, needing a decision (answered doesn't count), or
               any live human work; same tree, ancestors dim
    Human work  what waits on a person: decisions to make and your own to-dos (For you), grouped
               by project; whatever holds an AI up comes first (◆ bold, or a to-do other work is
               after), then ★, then the rest
    Waiting    everything delayed: waiting on someone or something outside (purple), or put off
               to a day or indefinitely (grey); due waits first, then by the day each comes back
    Live       every change, by anyone — a note, progress, an answer, a state change — newest first,
               finished and archived ones too; the last 30 days, older ones fold into "⏷ Older N"; h jumps here
    All        every node, including finished ones: finished children fold into one row,
               "✓ Completed N"; finished top-level nodes fold into "✓ Finished N" at the end of each
               project, +/- expands/collapses

  Delay (d)   one idea for both kinds of later. Type a day and, if it waits on someone or
              something, who or what: "fri Carol to confirm". Naming someone makes it an active
              wait (purple); a day alone, or nothing, a passive delay (grey). Both stay in Available
              and Waiting; when the day comes they go back to their usual colour, with a reminder.
              d again lifts it

  The numbers on the tabs: how many in Available/Active/Human work/Waiting; with external sources,
  a line under the tabs says whether they're clear.

  Status   ○ to do  ◐ running (red = asked 3× for a status update, no reply)
           ⏸ waiting outside
           ◇ human work: your own to-do, not started yet (replaces the status shapes above)
           ⬖ human work, started: the same to-do, in progress (also replaces the status shapes above)
           ◆ needs a decision: bold yellow = AI stuck, dim yellow = can decide early
           ✓ completed  ✕ closed
           ⚑ milestone: a goal with sub-goals under it, never started or finished on its
             own (m marks/unmarks it); the badge on the right shows children done/total
           ★ important — first in every list; ! marks or unmarks important
           ✎ a brief you filed, waiting for an AI to pick it up; the line under the tabs shows
             ● a session listening in the project / ○ none
           green = answered, awaiting an AI (you answered, an AI hasn't picked it up): shape
           unchanged — a decision stays ◆, a task stays ○ / ◐
  ◆ at the start of a row   something below (in the sub-nodes) needs a decision
  ▸ / ▾   a node with children, collapsed / expanded; +N is how many are hidden
  Progress  ████░░ 60% 3 minutes ago; red = asked 3× for a status update, no reply
  Previous rounds   a node asked again (a 2nd 选项 block) shows its earlier round(s) in the detail
                 pane, which one was picked and by whom — history only, the options below are what
                 you answer now

  ↑ / ↓          previous / next node
  ← / →          (tree) collapse / expand; already collapsed, ← jumps to the parent; already
                 expanded, → enters the first child; nothing left to expand, → enters the body's
                 image picker instead (same as i)
  - / +          (Available, Active, All) collapse / expand the node under the cursor, or a
                 "✓ Completed N" row; remembered, so it's the same next time you open bench
                 (stored in $NODDIT_HOME/bench-state.json, one per person; ← / → also remember it)
  w              jumps to the next decision an AI is stuck on (by urgency)
  g (or :)       type a number to jump (64, W305, web:305 all work), ⏎ jumps, Esc cancels; if it's
                 not in the current view, bench switches and expands it automatically; a ref that
                 doesn't resolve is tried as a title match instead, same as the app's own palette
  d              delays the node under the cursor (asks until when, and on what), or lifts its
                 delay; recorded as owner. An AI working on a passive delay is told "owner
                 deferred" and leaves it alone until it comes back
  D              「delay R days」: puts the node off to today + its R (nod edit --every 3d)
  s              starts this node (running now); already running, decided, or finished says so
  j / k          scroll the body down / up one line; Ctrl-F / ^B a screen, Ctrl-D / ^U half a
                 screen, Home / G (End) to the top / bottom
  1-9            answers by option number (asks to confirm first, you can add a note); pressing a
                 digit again on an answered node changes the answer
  ⏎              answers with this node's written default
  nodes with sub-questions   1 = all defaults; 2 = step through: ↑↓ change question, ←→ or the
                 option key to pick, n writes a change, ⏎ submit
  N              adds a reply (recorded as human · owner); it doesn't count as an answer, but the
                 node goes back to an AI
  Ctrl-A         while writing a reply (N) or an answer (confirming with a note): stages one or more
                 space-separated file paths (or URLs) to attach once it's sent — 📎N on the prompt
                 line counts what's staged; Esc there goes back to typing without losing the draft
  @              flips who does it: your own to-do becomes an AI’s (a request, heard the same way
                 nod assign ai from the owner is); an AI’s own node becomes your to-do
  m              flips whether this node is a milestone — the third kind, alongside human/AI;
                 turning it on clears whatever it was assigned to, off is the same as nod assign ai
  p / P          new brief for an AI: under the selected node / at its project's top level; a few
                 words, ⏎ files it; if no AI session is listening, asks whether to open one (y/n)
  ⇥ (in the p / P prompt)  cycles the new node's kind: a brief for an AI to expand and confirm →
                 a to-do for you (Human work, no AI works on it) → a task an AI can just do,
                 no expand-and-confirm step → back to a brief
  P with more than one project open  asks which project first (digit or ↑↓ then ⏎, Esc cancels)
  T              retitles this node (the prompt starts with its current title); ⏎ saves,
                 Esc cancels, clearing it does nothing
  E / e          opens $VISUAL / $EDITOR (vi if neither is set) on the description (E) or your own
                 latest reply (e) — a real file on disk, same as a git commit message; saving goes
                 through the same change-since-you-opened-it check nod edit uses, asking to
                 overwrite or drop it if something else wrote to this node meanwhile
  A              archives this node: already decided (you answered, an AI hasn't picked it
                 up) marks it completed right away, doesn't go in the queue; otherwise asks
                 why first (not doing it; blank = obsolete)
  M              move mode: ↑/↓ moves the node among the ones listed with it (siblings in a tree,
                 its group in a list), ⏎ or Esc when done; written as soon as it moves
  Space          marks / unmarks the node under the cursor (• at the row's start); with any
                 marked, d D s @ ! A act on every marked node; Esc clears the marks
  images in the body   each image is one row, 🖼️ name — right where its message put it,
                 whether inline or attached
  i              enters the body's image picker: ↑/↓ picks in reading order (scrolls there
                 automatically), i again (or ⏎/Space) opens the full-size view, O opens it in the
                 system viewer, ← / Esc goes back to the list; Z (condensed) only selects among the
                 images actually shown
  in the full-size view   ←/→ previous / next image (every image on this node, says so at either
                 end); +/- zoom, arrow keys pan once zoomed in, 0 resets, O opens in the system
                 viewer, q / Esc back to the body, keeps whichever image you were on
  o / O          o views an attachment (an image opens full-size in the terminal, anything else
                 goes to the system); O always opens it in the system viewer; several attachments
                 ask for a digit first
  H              opens this node's HTML attachment in a browser
  l / L          switches to the terminal window/tab running this node's project (iTerm2 / macOS
                 Terminal only, same as nod session goto); says so if there's no session to switch to
  Ctrl-L         the header's own Main agent dot: goes to its terminal if it's live, or starts
                 one if it's offline (same as nod session goto --main / nod session start --main)
  t              starts an agent session in this node's project (same as nod session start);
                 refuses if a lead is already listening there, saying who
  ;              opens Projects — ↑↓ picks, ⏎ renames, ←→ changes the letter (refused on a clash),
                 u unlinks it (its decisions/ stay on disk, nod projects add brings it back), or pick
                 「+ Add project」 and type a folder; ; or Esc closes it
  ,              opens Settings — language, right-to-left text, mouse, …; , or Esc closes it
  c              opens the Nod calendar — a text heatmap of the last year behind ⚡, weeks as
                 columns, weekdays as rows; c or Esc closes it
  v              opens Views — ↑↓ picks, ⏎ edits its fields, a adds one, x deletes it (the last
                 one stays), m moves it among the others; v or Esc closes it
  Z              condense/expand the body      R re-read from disk      q quit

  Mouse: click a tab name to switch, a node on the left to select it, an option to answer, an
         attachment to open it, a 🖼️ row to view it full-size;
         the wheel/trackpad scrolls whichever pane it's over, one row at a time; the left pane
         only scrolls the list, it doesn't change the selection.
  In the body, a paragraph starting "{{user}} | …" is yours (magenta); one starting "{{agent}} | …" is an
  AI's record (blue).

  press any key to go back

noteText.deferred: Later. Leave it alone until it’s resumed.
noteText.dependencyDone: {{ref}} is done and this node’s decision was already collected, so work starts now.
